candidate_answer: vLLM maps a request's logical KV blocks to physical memory through a block table that records the corresponding physical blocks and filled positions. It does not reserve all future token positions in advance, allowing dynamic allocation.

The KV block manager also maintains block tables—the mapping between logical and physical KV blocks of each request. Each block table entry records the corresponding physical blocks of a logical block and the number of filled positions. Separating logical and physical KV blocks allows vLLM to dynamically grow the KV cache memory without reserving it for all positions in advance, which eliminates most memory waste in existing systems, as in Fig. 2.
